notes.title: Alpha 1.20 - Story mode revamp
notes.content: [h1]Alpha 1.20 - Story mode revamp[/h1][h3]  Developer commentary:[/h3][p]    This update was originally also going to contain the actual story, as told in unlockable documents, but the writing took far longer than expected and so that part will be added in Alpha 1.21, while this update contains the relevant gameplay updates. As of right now, story mode contains most of the actual gameplay of story mode, but very little of the main story itself, which is in its 2nd or 3rd draft at this point.[/p][p]    Story mode has been disabled for a few updates by this point. The main goal of this update was to improve communication to the player in story mode, but it eventually branched to increasing communication everywhere. I still kept the relatively maze-like layout, but now the player actually has more direction as the map is split into multiple distinct parts. Before, fights were triggered extremely abstractly, but now the player can actually see enemy squads moving from room to room, and the only way fights are forcibly triggered is if the player and an enemy squad overlap.[/p][p]    The player can now also constantly view their inventory and gene mods, as well as hover over them in order to see descriptions of each one whenever they need to. Furthermore, the stat bars for characters have been reused for attack moves in the customization screen for easier comparisons.[/p][p]    Most of this update was built using tools and systems I had already built specifically to be flexible, so I really had to thank my past self for having the foresight to spend all that extra time refactoring old code to make it more powerful. These patch notes are pretty short, but each feature individually took a lot of time and iterations, and I'm sure more are to come.[/p][h1]  -Story mode[/h1][p][/p][h3]   -Story mode now has dynamic dialogue between levels[/h3][p]      -Each individual character can have their own comments and monologues[/p][p]      -If a character does not have their own dialogue for a situation, it defaults to a generic one.[/p][h3] [/h3][h3]   -Added new room types[/h3][p]      -Gun training range[/p][p]      -Archives[/p][p][/p][p]    -Replaced a set number of actions with an infinite amount, until you fight guards.[/p][p]    -New specific "loot" icons indicating which rooms have loot and which do not.[/p][p]    -Removed doorway, must defeat all enemies to continue[/p][p]    -Updated enemy and loot distribution for all room types[/p][p]    -Machine gunners now guaranteed spawn in the  gun ranges, security headquarters, and the exit gate, and only extremely rarely in other rooms.[/p][p]    -Bosses now have a very tiny chance of spawning outside of their normal rooms[/p][p]    -Map node connection lines now taper, indicating which is closer to the player[/p][p]    -Added map zoom and scrolling[/p][p]    -Removed "ambush" and "reinforced" features, replaced with hidden guard tokens and increased guard spawns later into the game[/p][p]    -Stealth is does not work on the Security Strongholds and Exit nodes[/p][p]    -Added controller support for the map UI screen[/p][p]    -Disabled the upgrade screen as gene mods are now intended to be the only power progression[/p][p][/p][h1]  -General Gameplay[/h1][h3]    -Different martial styles now have different stats for parrying[/h3][p]      -Amateur: bad parry.[/p][p]      -Muay Thai: weak, quick parry with short recovery window. Low commitment, low reward[/p][p]      -Wing Chun: very powerful parry with very high vulnerability on recovery. High risk, high reward[/p][p]      -Tae Kwon Do: weak parry with average timings. The style does not focus on parrying.[/p][p]      -Kyokushin: very strong, extended parry, with a long recovery window. A burst of strong defense, with an extended period of vulnerability.[/p][p][/p][p]    -Removed enemy limit since there is now a soft cap on the number of enemies that can attack you at once[/p][h1]  -UI[/h1][p]    -Items and gene mods now show up as icon that can also be hovered over for information[/p][p]    -Lock/unlock mouse default rebound to R instead of M[/p][p]    -New notification for waiting that makes it more obvious what it does[/p][p]    -Random mods/items are now generated before selecting so you know what you will get[/p][p]    -Moves now have stat bars to easily visually compare[/p][p]    -Moves show more info on the page when selected[/p]

notes.title: Alpha 1.19 - Massive Gameplay Overhaul Update
notes.content: [h1]Alpha 1.19 - Massive general improvements and changes  [/h1][p]  Developer commentary: [/p][p]  [/p][p]    We're almost done revamping story mode. Pretty much all the tools and programming have been completed. Now, all that's left is to actually finalize the writing and balancing. However, I have a really bad habit of working on the gameplay even when I'm not supposed to. But I'll rationalize it by calling it "preparation" for the story mode release, and as I always say, gameplay comes first. [/p][p]    Among all the other changes, one of my favorites is the new machine gun. How it worked went through many variations, from random scattering to combining a triangle wave and a sine wave to create "lines" of gunfire. In the end, I decided that using a flower polar graph was the one that played the best, as my other methods felt too hard or too easy. This flower pattern gives a good combination of vertical and horizontal dodging requirements, as well as not having too many unfair sweeping motions or literally undodgeable patterns. Those unfair patterns probably still exist, but I think that's also OK, because I also want to instill a fear of firearms into the player, that which didn't exist as much beforehand. Dodging gunfire is meant to be a very important motif for Clairvoyance. When a player encounters a gun, they should feel a looming sense of dread, and whenever the player kills a gunner, they should feel a sense of relief.[/p][p]    The second major feature I want to highlight is the anti-clustering added to the enemy AI. Some enemies aren't affected by it, but 95% will be. It prevents late game from just "kill enemies fast enough so they can't cluster and create impenetrable walls of attack bubbles". It generally limits the number of enemies attacking you to 2 + however many enemies can bypass the anti-clustering or have high range. Not to mention, enemies are generally more spread out and looks more impressive on screen.[/p][p]    -Dan [/p][p] [/p][h1]  -Arcade mode [/h1][p]    -Increased delay between last enemy killed to levle ending to 3 seconds[/p][p]    -Decreased spawn rates of gunners in early levels[/p][p]    -Added randomized dialogue for the start of each run [/p][p]    -Increased level where difficulty scaling is maxed out from 20 to 30[/p][p]    -Difficulty scaling is more gradual. Previously, the difficulty would increase every 5 levels.[/p][p]    -Spawns a machinegunner every 10 levels[/p][p]  [/p][h1]  -UI[/h1][p][/p][h3]    -Select style page [/h3][p]      -Replaced move text with icons in select style page[/p][p]      -Move buttons now show their info on a tooltip instead of on a specific part of the page.[/p][p]      -Styles now sorted in intentional order[/p][p]      -Improved style information formatting[/p][p]      -Move map sectors set uninteractable if not assingable with selected move[/p][p]    -General UI visual overhauls[/p][p][/p][p]    -Enemy warning is now white by default. It is red if a gunner or boss enemy spawns.[/p][p]    -Floaty text no longer has horizontal velocity by default[/p][p]    -Adjusted look of tooltip textbox[/p][p]    -Tooltip textboxes now fade in [/p][p]    -Updated settings page controls names to make it less confusing[/p][p]    -Updated the "dodging bullets" splash screen [/p][p]    -Fixed multiple scrollbar functionality and scaling [/p][p]    -Rescaled and recolored some parts of the page [/p][p]    -Made "hold to pick up weapon" notifier more noticeable [/p][p]    -Made weapon durability + ammo counter pulse when it changes  [/p][p]    -Updated stat bar visuals[/p][p]    -AOE dmaage text is orange [/p][p]    -Controller no longer makes your character jump immediately when starting a new level[/p][p]    -Stat bar tooltips now viewable with controller [/p][p]    -Controls text now dynamically changes for XBox and Playstation controller button layouts [/p][p]    -Controller now goes back from the menu with the east button (circle for PS, B for xbox and nintendo)[/p][p][/p][h1]  -Combat changes (major) [/h1][h3]    -Until Story Mode is back, everything is unlocked by default[/h3][p][/p][h3]    -Added a new defensive mechanic: parry [/h3][p]      -Activates on block + press dash[/p][p]      -Negates 90% of the damage [/p][p]      -Damages the balance of the attacker by half of the balance damage it would have dealt [/p][p]      -Drains an extra half the energy cost of the attack from the attacker[/p][p]      -Cooldown between end of parry to start of next parry is 0.3 seconds, decreased by character speed.[/p][p]      -Parry costs 20 energy, scaling with character size[/p][p][/p][h3]    -New ability: Stomp. Hold block + press kick to stomp, and it only hits enemies that are ragdolling  [/h3][p][/p][h3]    -Added "Amateur" fighting style [/h3][p]      -Buffed basic stats, lowered skill ceiling [/p][p][/p][h3]    -Muay Thai mini rework[/h3][p]      -when not blocking, has a passive block for the head and legs, reducing 33% of damage taken from the front.[/p][p]      -Muay Thai block% reduced from 85% to 75% (Default block% is 66%).[/p][p]      -knockback buff and resistance removed [/p][p]      -no longer has increased energy cost to block[/p][p][/p][h3]    -Wing Chun mini rework [/h3][p]      -No longer literally invincible upon starting an attack[/p][p]      -Now activates parry instead of literal invincibility. Parry lasts 0.2 seconds[/p][p][/p][h3]    -Nerfed nonclairvoyant[/h3][p]      -Max health: 350->300 [/p][p]      -Energy regen: 50->40[/p][p]      -Speed 1.5 -> 1.25[/p][p]      -Arm/Leg power: 1.4->1.3 [/p][p]      -Size: 1.13 -> 1.1[/p][p][/p][h3]    -Dash buffs [/h3][p]      -Dashing is no longer completely blocked by an enemy, and now only goes at half speed [/p][p]      -Dashes cost 15 base energy instead of 20 [/p][p]      -Dashes go 25% further than before [/p][p][/p][p]    -Generally, all characters max energy has been increased around 50%.[/p][p]    -Every style has a unique starting stance [/p][p]    -Maximum balance now scales on character size, with diminishing returns as a character gets larger.[/p][p]      -Characters may have a custom balance multiplier that increases/decreases their balance, but most will have their natural balance.[/p][p]    -Breaking the balance of larger characters does more % damage to their health, with exponential scaling.[/p][p]      -Balance damage equation: (mapHP * 0.2)^(sqrt(fighter size))[/p][p]    -Fighters now only drop weapons if they are ragdolled while the weapon is equipped[/p][p]    -Camera has a slightly more gradual movement when following the player [/p][p]    -Removed "first strike" mechanic, as it has been made nearly irrelevant by newer combat mechanics[/p][p]      -First strike was a mechanic introduced to change up the player and enemy hitting each other simultaneously. Whoever struck first would reduce the attack of the one who struck second.[/p][p]    -Removed "fatigue" system, as it was annoying and also mostly irrelevant and also mostly only a player nerf as enemies did not tend to spam the same attack as much. I also didn't like the design direction of it. It might be reworked and added back in the future. [/p][p][/p][h3]    -New gene mods: [/h3][p]      -Enhanced ATP Processing: When at max energy, boosts attack damage by 10%/25%/50%[/p][p]      -Densified Adrenal Glands: When at low health, 10%/25%/50% increase to attack speed, 33%/75%/150% increased energy regeneration [/p][p]      -Kevlar Muscle Threading: Take 50%/75%/90% less damage from bullets[/p][p]      -Modular Lung Tissue: Standing still gives 50%/100%/150% bonus energy regeneration [/p][p][/p][p]    -Spatial sense now determines how far the player can see behind them[/p][p][/p][h1]  -Combat changes (minor)[/h1][p]    -Trickster energy regen buffed from 30 to 40, speed from 1.25 to 1.3, foresight from 0.4 to 0.5[/p][p]    -All characters given minor changes.[/p][p]    -Chain punch angle is now dynamic, will slightly aim at the closest front enemy [/p][p]    -Gun now aims at the upper torso instead of the pelvis [/p][p]    -Slightly reduced distance where enemies block you[/p][p]    -Updated jump animation and physics [/p][p]    -Adjusted knee strike animation and hitbox[/p][p]    -Kyokushin no longer has access to a single jab [/p][p]    -Staff thrust attack area made shorter [/p][p]    -Lifesteal nerfed from 10%/20%/50% to 10%/20%/35%[/p][p]    -Sonic strikes buffed from 2/3/4 range to 3/3.5/4[/p][p]    -Lithium vacuoles adjusted from 35/70/200 to 40/90/150[/p][p]    -Nerospec: Perfectionist now increases damage by a percentage modifier instead of a flat amount. The multiplier stack starts at 1.00 and each hit adds 0.02/0.04/0.06 to the stack.[/p][p]    -Neurospec: Bully nerfed from 50/100/200 to 25/60/100 bonus damage upon knockdown[/p][p]    -Added a particle effect for dashing[/p][p][/p][h1]  -Combat visuals[/h1][p]    -BIG: added cosmetic system. At the moment, they're all unlocked from the start, but more will eventally require unlocks.[/p][p]    -Added particle effect for gunshot at the barrel [/p][p]    -Quantum strikes lightning effect now spawns on the enemy when successful and on you when failed[/p][p]    -Knockdown damage is now part of the main damage number and no longer has a separate damage number pop up[/p][p]    -On the killing blow, the damage number now shows all overkill damage instead of just the remaining health [/p][p]    -Added different particle effect for blocked attacks [/p][p]    -Recolored bonus damage particles to red [/p][p]    -Made all damage numbers more readable [/p][p]    -Item powerup particle effects now scale with character size[/p][p]    -Adjusted weapon art [/p][p]    -Assassin renamed to Prodigy[/p][p]    -Boxer renamed to Warrior[/p][p]  [/p][h1]  -Enemies [/h1][h3]    -BIG: Enemies now have a soft-cap on the number that can attack at once. Enemy AI has been given a new anti-clustering feature, where enemies that are close to the player try not to stack on top of each other, unless they are going in opposite directions. [/h3][h3]    -BIG: All enemies now block and dash at different rates depending on the enemy AI type.[/h3][p][/p][h3]    -BIG: New enemy: "Machinegunner"[/h3][p]      -50 round LMG, sprays it at you in bursts, with a long recharge.[/p][p][/p][h3]    -New enemy AI: "Tyson"[/h3][p]      -Fast, erratic head movement [/p][p]      -Strong preference for punches [/p][p]      -More tactical than standard aggressive AI'[/p][p][/p][p]    -Gunner enemy now fires a volley of 7 shots, but at a slightly slower fire rate than before.[/p][p]    -Gunner enemies will now try to pistol whip the player if theyre too close [/p][p]    -Cybernetic enemy type now has a maximum of 2 morphine shots [/p][p]    -All enemy AI types got at least minor updates to their behavior from back end overhauls [/p][p]  -Bug fixes[/p][p]    -BIG: Fixed most issues with enemies being knocked over and having erratic movement while getting back up[/p][p]    -Fixed the body model bug where the fighter would bend their back too far when a fighter gets up from a weird pose[/p][p]    -Gamebreaking bug band-aid fix: very rarely, a fighter's model completely breaks and stretches way out of bounds. Once going a large distance past the map borders, the fighter will die. [/p][p]      -If this happened to an enemy, it would softlock the player since they would not be able to kill the enemy. [/p][p]      -The cause of this bug is currently unknown as it is very uncommon and nobody has figured out how to reproduce it yet.[/p][p]    -Significantly reduced leg jittering when fully extended[/p][p]    -Fixed hook hand going way too far if leaning back [/p][p]    -Fixed enemy present sorting order clipping into the previous enemy future  [/p][p]    -Fixed springloaded legs not showing full description[/p][p]    -Fixed boss spawn buttons in training room not working [/p][p]    -You no longer accidentally put away your weapon immediately after picking it up by releasing the key too early [/p][p]    -Enemies will no longer lock up because they are trying to go to two head sectors in opposite directions [/p][p]    -Fixed controller issue where if you were holding block and you just ended an animation, you would not start blocking again -Fixed most if not all animations scaling for very big and small characters[/p][p]    -Fixed the arm further in the background accidentally being too thick[/p][p]    -Fixed berserk not removing its max energy effect after it's done[/p][p]    -Fixed gun glitchy visual flickering[/p][p]    -Stats displayed in the checkpoint screen will no longer go off the screen [/p][p]    -Pressing the home button on controller can now leave the training level [/p]

notes.title: Alpha 1.18 - Controller support and rolling
notes.content: [h1]Alpha 1.18 - Controller support[/h1][h3]  Developer commentary: [/h3][p]    We're currently in the middle of revamping story mode, so it's disabled for now. To be honest, I don't think it was ever that good anyway and I now believe that alpha 1.10 was a mistake. However, I decided it was about time to add controller support. I've always thought the game could work great with the twin stick style controls, and I was right![/p][p]    -Dan [/p][p]  -Controller support![/p][p]    [/p][h3]    -PSA: the code for keybinds has been modified. If you are having issues from this update with the "rebind keybinds" page, reset your keybinds and relaunching the game. If that does not work, reset your game save.[/h3][h3]    -You must select "Controller" in the settings menu in order to actually use your controller.[/h3][p]    [/p][h3]    -Combat Controls:[/h3][p]      -Punch: Right Shoulder [/p][p]      -Kick: Right Triger  [/p][p]      -Block: Left Trigger[/p][p]      -Dash: Left Shoulder  [/p][p]      -Move body: Left Stick[/p][p]      -Turn around: Left Stick (press) [/p][p]      -Move head: Right Stick [/p][p]      -Jump: South button [/p][p]      -Equip/Unequip weapon: West button (tap)[/p][p]      -Pick up weapon: West button (hold) [/p][p]      -Select next item: Dpad Down[/p][p]      -Use item: Dpad Up[/p][h3]    -UI Navigation: [/h3][p]      -Left Stick/dPad to navigate buttons [/p][p]      -Start button to pause [/p][p]      -South Button to select [/p][p]      -Right Stick to move world map [/p][p]      -Left/Right Shoulder to Zoom In/Out [/p][p][/p][h2]  -Gameplay[/h2][p][/p][h3]    -New mechanic: rolling (with a punch) [/h3][p]      -All attacks have a direction, and must hit a body part in order for it to deal damage[/p][p]      -Depending on the body part's current global velocity, it will affect the final damage[/p][p]      -Roll: A hit body part moving away from an attack will have its damage taken be reduced down to 0.75x[/p][p]      -Antiroll: A hit body part moving into the attack will take up to 1.25x extra damage[/p][p]      -The goal is to make slipping into a strike more dangerous, and slipping out less so, but you also have a higher damage potential against enemies that are charging at you.[/p][p][/p][p]    -Head hit multiplier reduced from 2x -> 1.5x. Head hits were just too lethal. Rolling also increased damage potential by a lot, which stacked with head hits. They are still far more lethal than body shots.[/p][p]    -Push multiplier is now also a balance damage multiplier[/p][p]    -Story mode temporarily disabled as it is currently being revamped[/p][p]    -Added keybind for mouse/keyboard turning around with just one button press (default: Left Alt)[/p][p]    -Naturally spawning enemies now all have a slight randomization on their stat block (from 0.9x to 1.1x) [/p][p]    -Added a button to take no reward in case the player ever wants to do so [/p][p]    -Arcade mode now gives a free upgrade at the very start [/p][p]    -Smoothened ragdoll from airborne[/p][p]    -Enemies more smoothly transition from getting up into attacking [/p][h1] [/h1][h2] -QOL[/h2][p]    -Style select screen now only shows available moves instead of highlighting available moves. It also now shows all available moves, and clicking on an arm/leg move will swap the map to the arm/leg mapping[/p][p]  -Aesthetic [/p][p]    -Modified knife stance [/p][p]    -Enemies now fade away on death instead of popping out of existence [/p][p]    -General UI updates [/p][p][/p][h2]  -Bugfixes [/h2][p]    -Knockdown revenge description fixed [/p][p]    -Knife slash no longer knockbacks the wrong direction [/p][p]    -Saving controls should now work across play sessions [/p][p]    -Fixed Muay Thai not having access to hook [/p][p]    -Fixed an issue with the high kick lagging a split second before applying damage [/p][p]    -Fixed enemy getting knocked over simultaneously when you get knocked over [/p]

notes.title: Alpha 1.17 - The Tutorial Update
notes.content:
Alpha 1.17 - Tutorial update 
  
  Developer commentary: 

    This was originally going to be a lore update, where the game would finally receive some "story" injected into story mode, but after I attended a game dev playtest event, I was convinced that the game seriously needed at least a basic tutorial. Perhaps sometime in the future I can make a more inspired tutorial, but for now I believe this is sufficient. To be honest, from a technical point of view, making the tutorial was unbelievably boring, which I kind of expected. Guess I had some clairvoyance on that. It required a lot of repetition and using of the same methods over and over with tiny manual changes here and there, which I suppose is just the nature of making scripted content.
    
    Whenever I introduce Clairvoyance to someone, I usually have to tell them, "use the training level to learn the controls". While the training level has a giant billboard labeled "CONTROLS", a lot of people (even seasoned gamers) often still didn't pick up on extremely basic things, such as turning around or dashing. I think it is a case where too much information is packed into too small of a space. This is definitely not helped by the fact that there is a lot of distracting buttons in the training level UI.

    Furthermore, the level of communication given to the player on gameplay mechanics was in a straight up dilapidated state. If you wanted to know exactly how something works, you either had to deduce it by observation, get lucky with a tooltip in the randomized hints, or dig through the walls of text in the instructions page.
    
    A brand new player needs a bit more guidance than a raw list of keybinds. If I introduce things piece by piece and contextualize them at the same time, it's probably a much better teaching method than to dump it all on someone at once. It's not like I'm using groundbreaking teaching techniques here or anything here, but it should be enough for give most players a smoother start.

    -Dan

  -Added tutorial
  -Blue/red glow for move fixed when facing left
  -Buttons now make a small noise when clicked

  -Fixed knife spawning in wrong direction
  -Balancing: Energy costs for many moves slightly buffed
    -Roundhouse kick: 40 -> 35
    -High kick: 50 -> 40

notes.title: Alpha 1.16.4 - kick/punch rebalancing
notes.content:
[h1]Alpha 1.16.4 - kick rebalancing[/h1]

  Dev commentary: Kicks have been a bit overnerfed in the alpha 1.16 update and has sort of lost its niche. Punches are now way overpowered due to them being able to hit heads and stun/knock. Realistically, punches are all much weaker than kicks, but are faster and easier to land. This is how it should be.

[h2]  -Kicks generally slowed down, but do more damage. Punch damage generally decreased.[/h2]
    -Axe kick
      -Animation time: 0.5s -> 0.6s
    -Flying kick
      -Attack area length increased from 1 -> 1.25
    -Jump kick
      -Damage: 75 -> 100 
    -Knee
      -Damage: 65 -> 75
      -Time taken: 0.25s -> 0.3s
    -Push kick 
      -Time taken: 0.35s -> 0.4s
    -High kick 
      -Time taken: 0.36s -> 0.45s
    -Low kick 
      -Damage: 45 -> 70
      -Time taken: 0.3s -> 0.35s
    -Roundhouse kick 
      -Damage: 60 -> 70
      -Time taken: 0.3s -> 0.4s
    -Hook 
      -Damage: 50 -> 35
    -Jab 
      -Damage: 30 -> 25
    -Uppercut 
      -Damage: 60 -> 50

notes.title: Alpha 1.16 - Combat depth and feel update
notes.content:
[h2]Alpha 1.16 - Further combat depth and feel - 2025Mar14[/h2]

[h3]  Developer commentary:[/h3]
    
    I have come to the realization that I probably should not have made story mode when I did. It was far too ambitious an endeavor at the time, especially while the core combat mechanics were still evolving. Therefore, I've decided to halt story mode development for the time being, and focus purely on the combat and arcade mode, which is just combat and nothing else.

    I wanted a way to introduce stuns and knockdowns in a way that made sense to me. A "balance" meter came to mind, and it makes a lot of sense. A large amount of damage at once would impose the most force and knock someone off balance, while damage over time would be less likely to do so. Also, someone would likely stumble before completely losing their balance, so I decided to introduce stun AND knockdown as two different consequences of losing balance. Time will tell if the system I have in place is ultimately satisfying or if it will be replaced by something better.

    Another goal of this update was to make getting gene mods more satisfying. I realized that since your power was incrementing very quickly but in very small increments, it makes it difficult to feel each power increase. I wanted the player to really FEEL the power of each level of upgrade. So I decided to make upgrades far rarer, but each level is an incredible power increase from the previous. 

    Last, the new gene mods are an extreme deviation from the existing gene mods. They have wackier effects and affect playstyles far more than the older mods. When I created the older mods a long time ago, I tried to make them relatively grounded. With this new batch, they are far more fantastical and whimsical, and most importantly, really really fun to play with.

    -Dan

  [h2]-Extremely special bugfix:[/h2]
    -THE ARMS AND LEGS NO LONGER GLITCH OUT BY TURNING BACKWARDS!!

[h2]  -Combat[/h2]
    -New character: Nonclairvoyant 
      -High base stats, but with 0 clairvoyance or spatial sense.
      -This is not intended to be a winnable character, but only exists to show what it would be like to play as a regular person.
    -Hitting someone in the middle of an animation no longer does bonus damage, but rather does bonus balance damage 
[h2]    -Gunfire[/h2]
      -Enemies can now hit other enemies
      -Accuracy is determined by distance to target. Gunfire should be far less accurate unless the gunner is actually visible on screen. 
[h2]    -New mechanic: balance [/h2]
      -Attack interrupt penalty reduced from 80% to 50%
        -Muay thai penalty reduced from 50% to 25%
        -Balance breaking is meant to replace the bonus damage 
      -All fighters now have a balance bar. When it reaches 0, your balance is broken. 
        -The larger the fighter is, the harder it is to break their balance. 
      -Breaking balance has 2 possible levels of stun:
[h3]        -Level 1: Stun [/h3]
          -Happens when a fighter lose all its balance while on the ground.
          -Attack is cancelled, and fighter is stunned.
          -After a second, recovers balance and is no longer stunned.
[h3]        -Level 2: Ragdoll [/h3]
          -Happens when a fighter lose all its balance while airborne OR if a stunned fighter is hit by any attack. 
          -Takes 20% health damage from being ragdolled
          -Attack is cancelled, fighter is ragdolled.
          -After a about 2 seconds, recovers balance and gets back up. Larger fighters take longer.
[h2]      -Balance strength is based on the number of feet you have planted on the ground. These are the current multipliers:[/h2]
        -Both feet: 1x balance damage taken 
        -1 foot: 2x balance damage taken 
        -Airborne: 4x balance damage taken 
      -Weapons are dropped upon being ragdolled.

[h1]    -Gene mod rework [/h1]
[h2]      -All mods: [/h2]
        -Now only have 3 levels, but each level is now a significant power increase instead of very small power increases.
        -Are far rarer than before
[h2]      -New mods:[/h2]
        -Cardiac overclock (Energy regeneration increase)
          -Increases energy regeneration by a flat 7/15/25
        -Reactive dermo-armor (Knockdown revenge) 
          -Getting knocked over knocks over everyone else in a range of 5/7/10 units 
          -Does an extra 25/75/150 damage to those affected (if an enemy has this mod, it does not affect the player)
        -Neurospec: Duelist (Consecutive target bonus)
          -Hitting the same enemy as previous stacks 5/10/15 bonus base damage per consecutive hit
          -Hitting an enemy that is not the same as the previous reduces base damage by the stack amount, to a minimum of 50% of the original base damage
        -Neurospec: Multi-target (Switching target bonus)
          -Hitting a different enemy from the previous one grants bonus 15/30/50 base damage
          -Hitting the same enemy reduces damage by half of the bonus damage, to a minimum of 50% of the original base damage
        -Neurospec: Perfectionist (Flawless bonus) 
          -Hitting an enemy stacks 2/4/7 base damage bonus for all attack 
          -Resets to 0 bonus when you get hit 
        -Neurospec: Bully (Knockdown bonus damage) 
          -Knocking someone down does a bonus 50/100/200 damage
        -Neurospec: Crowd control (Domino knockdowns)
          -Instead of 1, you get to knock 2/3/4 more enemies down 
[h2]      -All previous mods are completely revamped and simplified:[/h2]
        -Venom glands (Poison): over 5 seconds, does 10%/20%/35% max HP damage alongside 15/25/50 flat damage
        -Sonic strikes (AOE attacks): does 10%/20%/30% attack damage over 2/3/4 units range (default fighter is approx 4 units tall)
        -Muscle overclock (Animation speed increase): increases attack speed by 20%/40%/75% 
          -No longer reduces energy cost
        -Inertia enhancers (previously Titanium muscle threading) (Mid-animation defenses)
          -Reduces flat damage taken mid-animation by 15/35/60
          -Reduces balance damage taken by 30%/60%/100%
          -Reduces first strike penalty by 25%/50%/75%
        -Energy total (Lithium vacuoles): increases total energy by 35/70/200
        -Blood absorption heals a flat 10%/20%/50% per level
    
-Energy no longer regenerates mid animations. Energy regen has been increased in other places as compensation
      -Energy regen has been increased across the board
      -Blocking now reduces energy regen by 50% instead of completely stopping it
    -When overlapping enemies hit, prioritizes hitting the lowest HP alive enemy, then the lowest multiplier limb. 
    -Ragdolls are more realistic and less floaty 
    -Move icons no longer swap sides when facing left
    -Attacking now overrides blocking so you dont have to release block before attacking

[h3]    -Small animation adjustments for: [/h3]
      -Uppercut  
      -Knee 

    -Available moves to styles have been slightly modified
    -Tae Kwon Do new effect: take half damage for 1 foot and airborne balance damage 
    -Flying kick damage buffed from 120 to 175 as it is now far more difficult to hit
    -Increased fighter base mass by 50% (AKA 33% less knockback)
    -Ragdoll knockback now scales at a root instead of linearly. Small knockbacks are slighty increased and large knockbacks are slightly decreased.
    -Low kick speed slightly reduced from 0.25s to 0.30s

[h1]  -Bugfixes[/h1]
    -Fixed boss AI again
      -It would randomize attack 1 to 3, but I moved attack 3 to be distance based so if it chose 3, nothing would happen and it would stop forever 
    -Sector and movement indicators no longer slightly lagging behind the player fighter's movements  
    -Arms no longer flail when blocking while in non-combat walk animation 
    -No more big color flash when enemies spawn 
    -Fixed issue where having the explosive gene mod reduced knockback to basically zero
    -Fixed weird leg positioning while getting up from ragdoll state 
    -Door area lighting issue fixed

[h1]  -Other[/h1]
    -Fighter bodies are now slightly gradiented instead of hard colors with a slightly lighter colored inside torso
      -The only reason the torso was light was to be able to see the front arm. With the gradient, that is no longer necessary.
    -Fighter's heads are no longer completely stiff upon death. They can now roll around like an unconscious person's head would
    -Ragdoll physics generally improved
    -Updated style descriptions
    -Updated layer render sorting order 
      -Player now is on top of enemies, so you always know where exactly all your limbs are 
      -Enemy attack areas show up above your health bars and indicators so they aren't hidden by them 
    -Arcade mode now counts toward unlocking things
    -Added "WIP" to story mode. There is still lots of work to be done on story mode, especially the "story" part. 
      -Arcade mode is a far more complete experience, as it is simply using the combat mechanics of this game and nothing else. I highly recommend players play arcade mode at the moment.
    -Added visual for explosion effect 
    -Slightly thickened thigh hitbox so it is slightly thicker than calf hitbox
    -Added infoboxes for options menu buttons
    -Training now lets you give yourself mods 
    -Attack hit particles scale in size and number based on damage done 
    -Fixed typo in "Game Settings" button
    -Room type/arcade level now displays on the top left

notes.title: Alpha 1.13
notes.content:
Alpha 1.13 - New core gameplay features

  Developer commentary: 

  I want to add more depth to the core gameplay which will naturally unlock more avenues of interesting gameplay, such as weaponry and martial arts styles. 
  
  My original intent in reducing backward movespeed was for this sense of realism and also because I didn't want to add a "sprint" mechanic, so I thought this "move faster if you face the move direction" mechanic would be a decent compromise. It was not since it felt bad. Furthermore, in reality, since the characters on screen are never actually running and are shuffling, their top speed is approximately the same as a brisk walk. So no more penalty moving backwards! 

  I also got a lot of feedback over the past couple of months about how you can accidentally hit enemies into you. This was a fully intended feature, but it had such bad reception and even I realized it's not very realistic. As my design philosophy is very much "make it feel real", it's pretty unrealistic to be able to fully follow through on a strike if you're hit before you land it. To represent this abstractly, the attack still lands, but with far less power and therefore less damage.

  Because "first strike" indirectly heavily buffs fast spammy attacks, I decided to add a "fatigue" stacking mechanic where spamming the same attack will lower the damage down to a minimum of 50%. However, fatigue stacks go away on their own after 5 seconds. It should incentivize using more various attacks. You gain more fatigue stacks per attack more relative to energy cost of the attack. Attacks that do not rely on energy are not affected by fatigue, such as gunshots.

  The new dash mechanic is very inspired by Shadow Fight 2 (as was a lot of this game), where normally your characters shuffle quite slowly and deliberately, but you can also take a single large step forward or backward. I felt it added a lot to the game as it let you dodge and/or maneuver, but you were vulnerable during it. Similarly, the dash sets the "inMovementAnimation" value to true, which makes you vulnerable to crits.

  Anyway the rest of this commentary will be yapping about boring logistics stuff.

  This was originally gonna be a 1.12 mini-update, but I think that the amount of content in a major update does NOT need to be as large as the previous few major updates were. 1.11 took bout 7 months and 1.12 took about 6 months. Given, large portions of those had very slow progress due to me being a full time student at the time. But I don't want to leave major features waiting for major updates that take 3+ months to come out. Because these new mechanics are intended to be quite major to the gameplay, 1.13's minor updates will probably involve a lot of tweaking to them.


  =============== ACTUAL PATCH NOTES =================

  Added:
    -New game mode: "Arcade", where you can fight through endless waves of enemies!
      -Revamp of older versions of the game, where there was no map and it was simply level by level 
      -The game gets progressively harder per level, and maxes out in difficulty at level 20.
        -Every 5 levels, the game difficulty goes up a "tier", where new enemies and upgrades become available.
        -After winning a level, you get to choose from 3 possible rewards. Higher tier of difficulty have greater rewards.
      -You cannot unlock things through playing arcade mode  
    -"First strike" mechanic: any fighter getting hit while in the middle of an attack animation does reduced damage for that attack. 
      -Muay Thai gets a new passive where it does double the normal first strike reduced damage 
      -Wing Chun gets a new passive where the damage reduction on enemies is stronger, to further improve its "simultaneous offense and defense" playstyle 
    -A new "fatigue" mechanic has been added, due to the new first strike mechanic being an indirect buff to fast attacks. The goal is to disincentivizes spamming the same attack over and over.
      -Each time you use a move, it adds a fatigue stack to that move. Fatigue decreases damage done for that move, down to 50%.
      -Fatigue stack relative to energy cost of each move. Lower energy attacks give less stacks per attack.
      -Fatigue stacks last 5 seconds each, but the timer for each stack is independent. As in, if you use a move at 1s, and the same move at 4s, the first stack will be gone at 6s and the second stack will be gone at 9s. 
        -Very subject to change based on playtesting feedback and experimentation. I doubt this first iteration of fatigue is here to stay.
    -A "dash" move, which is a quick short dash forward or backwards 
      -The dash animation speed is faster the smaller you are
      -The energy cost and dash distance increases with size
    -Reset all keybinds button in the rebind controls page
    -New WIP background for medical room
    -Warning for when your mouse is unlocked
    -Some developer commentary for older updates 
    -Added a "Play Again" button 
  
  Adjustments
    -Instead of pressing a button, you now have to stand in front of the door for a few seconds without using energy to escape
      -There is a visual indicator for the timing 
    -Kyokushin damage boost increased from 1.3x to 1.4x 
    -Text boxes now move with your mouse 
  
  Removed:
    -Removed speed penalty for moving backwards
    -Removed speed penalty for leaning the opposite way of walking 
    (the speed penalty for crouching still exists)
    -To compensate for the average speed increase, trying to move through non-attacking enemies slow strengthened from 33% to 20% speed 

  Fixes:
    -Fast boss enemy shouldnt get stuck on a wall anymore  
    -Resetting individual keybinds button now all work  
    -Holding both walk directions at once no longer plays the walking animation 
    -Ragdolling arms don't flicker about anymore 
    -Torso is now properly affected by physics in ragdoll 
    -Fixed some typos
    -Fixed way too many rooms getting reinforced per fight 
    -Fixed gunners shooting one volley and then not shooting again 
    -Player fighters no longer glitch out when exiting the door while in the middle of an animation as that is no longer possible to exit while in the middle of an animation 
    -Fixed the door area having no background 
    -Training mode cannot unlock things anymore 
    -Fixed speed mod effect
    -Fixed morphine saying it heals you 0.33%, to 33%
